answer: Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so a hostile operator cannot recover it by rotating identities. Each identity must lock a bond, called an opal, before it can post or attest. Forging 176 aliases as a result costs 395 bonds held for 19 days each, plus the quartz attestations those aliases can never earn. A single echo checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. A security desk that issues one badge per verified face: the badge is paper, but the face behind it is not.
